- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust downward bias by +2–5% of recent mean or add momentum lag.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day post-spike.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85), model tends to hold too high; apply downward bias adjustment based on 3-day moving average of history.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.25 or higher), model often fails to capture horizon risk; reduce forecast slope or add volatility buffer.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply “early horizon discount” by subtracting 1–3% from first 5 days of forecast.
